name: Electric Bicycle
description: A device with a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal assist to 20 mph, throttle to 20 mph, or pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.13e)

Class 1: pedal assist only, ceasing at 20 mph; Class 2: propels it to 20 mph whether or not the rider pedals, cutting out when the brakes are applied; Class 3: pedal assist only, ceasing at 28 mph (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.13e)
Riders of a Class 3 must be 14 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
Riders and passengers under 18 on a Class 3 must wear a properly fitted and fastened CPSC- or ASTM-compliant bicycle helmet (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
Since January 1, 2018, manufacturers must permanently affix a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a, added by 2017 Public Act 139)

Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match; modified beyond the class limits, or with a motor over 750 watts, it's no longer an electric bicycle (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
Subject to the same rules as a bicycle and not a motor vehicle or moped: no driver's license, registration or insurance (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
Ridden on any part of a highway open to bicycles, including bike lanes and shoulders, and on sidewalks where bicycles are allowed (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
Barred from cities that ban nonemergency motor vehicles unless the city council allows it, and from Mackinac Island State Park without a permit from its commission (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)

Class 1 may use paved, crushed-limestone and rail trails unless the agency that manages the trail bans it; Class 2 and Class 3 may use them only if that agency allows it (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
Barred from nonmotorized natural-surface trails unless the agency that manages the trail allows it (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)
A local authority or state agency must hold a public hearing before it bans, allows or regulates e-bikes (Michigan Compiled Laws §257.662a)

On DNR land, Class 1 may use state park, recreation area and state forest trails open to bicycles (except state game and wildlife areas and some named pathways); Class 2 needs a free disability permit, and Class 3 is barred
